title: Second: no grace physically predetermines the will
source_text: CXX. Secundo pertendunt, cum eodem Molina, nullam Dei gratiam sic efficacem esse, ut voluntatem ad bene agendum Physice praedeterminet, & sic ut aliquam imponat agendi necessitatem, quae sit ad bonam ipsam actionem antecedens. Nec enim censent ullam talem necessitatem cum arbitrii humani libertate consistere posse. Quanquam alioqui non negent gratiam Physice movere & inclinare voluntatem ad bonas operationes.
pass_a_gloss: CXX. Secondly they contend, with the same Molina, that no grace of God is so efficacious, as to predetermine the will Physically to acting well, & so as to impose some necessity of acting, which is antecedent to the good action itself. For they do not think that any such necessity can consist with the liberty of human choice. Although otherwise they do not deny that grace Physically moves & inclines the will to good operations.
pass_b_english: Thesis CXX. Second, they maintain with Molina that no grace of God is efficacious in the sense of physically predetermining the will to act well and so imposing a necessity of acting that comes before the good action itself. In their view no such necessity can coexist with the freedom of human choice. They do not deny, on the other hand, that grace moves and inclines the will physically toward good operations.
